question: Can LLMs reason effectively without prompting, and to what extent?
hypothesis: CoT reasoning paths are inherent in pre-trained LLMs' top-k alternative decoding paths and are hidden by greedy decoding; a CoT in the path correlates with higher answer confidence.
contributions: LLMs can reason by simple decoding changes, without prompting
The method gives a view of intrinsic reasoning ability without human priors from prompts
CoT-decoding selects CoT paths by answer confidence, improving over greedy decoding

method.summary: At the first decoding step, branch over the top-k tokens (k=10), continue greedy decoding on each branch, then pick the path (or aggregate answers across paths) with the highest answer confidence, defined as the mean top-1 minus top-2 probability margin over answer tokens. Input is the plain 'Q: [question]\nA:' format with no CoT prompt.
method.task: reasoning decoding (math, commonsense, symbolic) without prompts

datasets.name: GSM8K
datasets.split: test set (Table 7); first 100 questions for the manual CoT analysis and Table 2 ('top-100')

datasets.name: Year parity
datasets.source: names from Berglund et al. 2023 reversal-curse list; task from Allen-Zhu and Li 2023
datasets.preprocessing: For Mistral, ground-truth year is what Mistral-7B itself returns when asked the birth year; names with no retrievable year dropped (<2% on inst-tuned)

datasets.name: Coin Flip, Web of lies, Multi-step arithmetic (synthetic)
datasets.size: 100 examples per difficulty level, except Web-of-Lies (5) which uses the existing dataset
datasets.source: Wei et al. 2022; Big-Bench-Hard (Suzgun et al. 2022)

models.name: PaLM-2 (XS, Small, Medium, Large; pre-trained and inst-tuned)

inference.decoding: CoT-decoding: top-k tokens at first step, then greedy continuation; select max-Delta path or aggregate by sum of Delta per answer
inference.max_tokens: PaLM-2: input length 256, max decode steps 128 (CoT-decoding); few-shot input 1024, output 256 for few-/zero-shot CoT. Mistral: 200 new tokens pre-trained / 400 inst-tuned on math; 50 / 100 on year parity
inference.samples: k=10 paths per question (default); single run, no seeds stated
inference.prompting: Q: [question]\nA: (multi-step arithmetic uses raw input, e.g. '3+5-6='); Mistral inst-tuned: '[INST] question [/INST]'

parameters.Delta: mean over answer tokens of p(x1_t|x<t) - p(x2_t|x<t)
parameters.aggregation: answer a maximizing sum over paths of Delta_k,a
parameters.answer_span: last number / final option (Mistral); PaLM-2: extend output with 'So the answer is' and align
parameters.ill_formed_filter: drop empty, max-length, question-mark-ending responses and (Mistral) training-data-like text
parameters.binary_tasks: Coin Flip/Web of Lies: difference of probability mass over yes/true vs no/false

other.compute: Mistral/Gemma: A100 40GB, ~10-20 hours per task; PaLM-2: TPU v4, a few hours to a few days per job

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of questions with correct final answer from the selected path

eval.protocol: Single configuration per cell; no seeds, variance or significance tests reported.

availability.weights: public Mistral and Gemma HF models; PaLM-2 not public

limits: Extra compute: k decoded paths per question (O(k)) versus O(1) for greedy (Table 7)
Confidence (top-2 margin) may be less precise for open-ended answers (Sec 5)
Branching only at the first token; later branching not explored
Gains shrink on more synthetic/complex tasks; correct CoT paths rarer at 3+ step manipulation
With zero-shot CoT prompting, PaLM-2 L GSM8K (75.1) beats prompt-free CoT-decoding (63.2)
Only three model families, PaLM-2 not public; single run, no variance reported
Year-parity ground truth for Mistral comes from the model's own birth-year answers
Pre-trained and instruction-tuned models only, all pre-2024 (PaLM-2, Mistral-7B v0.1, Gemma-7B); no reasoning-trained models
